steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Media representations of crime: the media over-represent violent and sexual crime (12% actual but 60-70% media coverage). The media under-represent corporate and white-collar crime. This distortion creates a false public perception. | Key Fact: Moral panics (Cohen): a condition where the media defines a group as a threat to societal values. Cohen's mods and rockers study: media exaggerated minor beach fights, creating a moral panic that labelled them as 'folk devils'. | Key Fact: Deviancy amplification spiral: media exaggeration -> increased public concern -> increased policing -> more arrests -> more media coverage -> further exaggeration. The spiral makes the 'problem' appear bigger than it really is. | Key Fact: Fear of crime: media coverage increases fear, especially among vu

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe Cohen's concept of moral panics and evaluate its usefulness. | Explain how the media distorts the public's perception of crime. | Evaluate whether media coverage of crime causes more harm than the crime itself.
